intro: Here is Cendere Bridge, in Adıyaman province, built in the late 2nd century AD. This Roman bridge crosses the Cendere in a single arch. Of the four columns raised by the XVI Legion for Septimius Severus and his family, three still stand.
history: The bridge was built at the end of the second century AD by the XVI Legion, together with the surrounding Commagenian cities, for the emperor Septimius Severus, his wife Julia Domna and their sons. Three of the four columns still stand. And the fourth? It belonged to Geta, and it was taken down after he was murdered and his name struck from the record.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the single arch span and the Severan columns. Look for the dedicatory inscription, and follow the remains of the Roman road.
facts: Did you know? The bridge has stood for eighteen centuries and carried vehicles until recently; traffic stopped only when a new bridge was built beside it. One of its four columns is missing: when Geta's name was struck from the record after his death, his column came down with it. And because the bridge sits on the road up to Mount Nemrut, most Commagene itineraries cross it.
outro: This brings our tour of Cendere Bridge to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Safe travels on the road ahead, and enjoy your visit.
